text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government names renowned journalist Peter Enahoro as chief executive of the majority state-owned New Daily Times .
- Federal government establishes interministerial council on chemical weapons, to sensitise the chemical industry to its obligations under international treaties.

- Over two million tonnes of paper left unsold at Iwopin Pulp and Paper Company (IPCCL) on weak consumer demand. IPCCL's attempt to cut prices to 75,000 naira per tonne from 130,000 has failed to stimulate demand.
- Five Nigerian vessels seized by British authorities to settle creditors after the failure of Nigerian National Shipping Lines may be auctioned soon.
- Chief of General Staff Lieutenant General Oladipo Diya says Failed Banks Decree will be made "more humane". Dozens of directors of failed banks have been detained under the decree.
- Kaduna and Katsina states in northern Nigeria are contesting central bank plans to liquidate and sell the Nigeria Universal Bank which they jointly own.
- Owners of marginal oil fields who have refused to exploit them for 10 years may be compelled to release them to new investors.
